education_responses.student: I will arrange breathing tests and a chest image rather than assuming the cough is just from past smoking. We will review the results in two weeks. Sudden severe breathing trouble or coughing blood needs earlier help.
education_responses.patient: Thank you. I understand that the next steps depend on the examination and tests.

education_responses.student: We can look for an appointment that limits lost work time and coordinate transport with your daughter if you wish.

differentials.name: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
differentials.teaching_context: Chronic productive cough, progressive exertional dyspnea and smoke exposure support COPD; spirometry is needed.

differentials.name: Bronchiectasis
differentials.teaching_context: Daily sputum and recurrent infections support this alternative; imaging is required and infection history is not proof of cause.

differentials.name: Lung malignancy
differentials.teaching_context: Persistent symptoms, age and smoking exposure warrant exclusion despite no hemoptysis or weight loss.

model_note.S:
CC: I cough up mucus every morning and get winded more easily.

HPI: 56-year-old male. Productive cough for 2 years. Several tablespoons of white morning sputum. Symptoms most days year-round. Progressive exertional dyspnea over 6 months; now stops after one flight. No resting or conversational dyspnea. Diffuse exertional breathing discomfort. 25 years of loading-dock diesel exposure. Worse with exertion, smoke and cold air. Rest relieves dyspnea; expectoration temporarily clears mucus. Cough syrup ineffective; no inhaler use. Two treated chest infections in 3 years.

PMH: Hypertension; no established lung diagnosis.

PSH: Cholecystectomy at 42.

Meds: Amlodipine 5 mg daily.

SH: Former smoker: 32 pack-years, quit 2 years ago. Four beers weekly. No recreational drugs. Delivery driver; limited during unloading. Lives alone; daughter can transport; visits cause lost pay.

FH: Father: lung cancer at 68; father smoked. Mother: hypertension; brother: no known major illness.

Allergies: No known drug allergies.

ROS: Respiratory: Intermittent expiratory wheeze. No hemoptysis. No recent sputum volume or color change. General: No fever. No weight loss. No night sweats. Cardiovascular: No chest pain. No orthopnea. No edema.
model_note.O:
Vitals: BP 132/80 mmHg, P 82 bpm, R 18 rpm, T 98.1 F oral, Pulse Ox 95% on room air, Ht 5' 9", Wt 178 lbs

General: Comfortable at rest, speaking full sentences.
Lungs: Symmetric chest expansion; no accessory muscle use at rest. Breath sounds mildly reduced bilaterally with prolonged expiration and scattered expiratory wheezes; no focal crackles. Mildly increased resonance symmetrically over posterior fields.
Heart: Regular rate and rhythm without murmur.
Extremities: No peripheral edema, digital clubbing or cyanosis.
Osteopathic: T4 bilateral thoracic paraspinal tissue texture change and tenderness.
P: 1. Obtain post-bronchodilator spirometry and chest radiograph; assess symptoms and exacerbation history. If COPD is confirmed, select inhaled bronchodilator therapy and teach technique; review vaccination and continued smoking abstinence. Arrange review in 2 weeks around work. Acute breathlessness, confusion or blue lips needs emergency care.

2. If sputum/infection history or initial imaging remains concerning, arrange thin-section chest CT and sputum studies when indicated; respiratory referral can guide airway clearance. Explain infection warning signs and avoid empiric long-term antibiotics.
3. Investigate persistent cough with diagnostic chest imaging and escalate suspicious findings to a lung specialist promptly. Discuss that risk is not a diagnosis and reinforce smoking abstinence.
